Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the 24 * rule for deciding when two owners denote the same person lives in one place, as pure functions 25 * with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, 26 * {@link EmailNormalizer} and {@link HouseholdNormalizer}, whose comparison keys it composes. 27 * 28 *

The key is the owner's normalized telephone, email (or the empty string when absent) and 29 * household id joined with {@code '|'} separators: 30 * {@code normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId}. Two owners are the same, and a 31 * create is rejected as a {@code 409 Conflict}, only when their whole keys are equal — so the 32 * previously separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are all subsumed by this one 33 * key. Because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same 34 * {@code householdId}) with different telephones have different keys and are both allowed; only an 35 * exact full-key match is a duplicate. 36 */ 37 public abstract class OwnerIdentity { 38 39 /** Separates the telephone, email and household components of the key. */ 40 private static final String SEPARATOR = "|"; 41 42 /** 43 * Builds the identity key from an owner's raw parts. The telephone and email are reduced to 44 * their {@linkplain TelephoneNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} / 45 * {@linkplain EmailNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} forms so values stored in different 46 * shapes still compose equal keys; an absent (null or blank) email contributes the empty string, 47 * and an absent household id likewise contributes the empty string. 48 * 49 * @param telephone the owner's telephone (normalized on create), or null 50 * @param email the owner's email (lower-cased on create), or null/blank when absent 51 * @param householdId the owner's household id, or null 52 * @return the owner's identity key 53 */ 54 public static String identityKey(String telephone, String email, String householdId) { 55 String telephonePart = telephone == null ? "" : TelephoneNormalizer.toComparisonKey(telephone); 56 String emailPart = (email == null || email.isBlank()) ? "" : EmailNormalizer.toComparisonKey(email); 57 String householdPart = householdId == null ? "" : householdId; 58 return telephonePart + SEPARATOR + emailPart + SEPARATOR + householdPart; 59 } 60 61 /** 62 * Builds the identity key from a persisted owner's stored telephone, email and household id. 63 * 64 * @param owner the owner (non-null) 65 * @return the owner's identity key 66 */ 67 public static String identityKey(Owner owner) { 68 return identityKey(owner.getTelephone(), owner.getEmail(), owner.getHouseholdId()); 69 } 70 71 } 72

1 /* 2 * Copyright 2016-2017 the original author or authors. 3 * 4 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); 5 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. 6 * You may obtain a copy of the License at 7 * 8 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 9 * 10 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software 11 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, 12 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. 13 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and 14 * limitations under the License. 15 */ 16 17 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util; 18 19 import java.util.Locale; 20 21 /** 22 * Comparison of owner households, an owner's {@code lastName} together with their {@code postcode}. 23 * Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the rule for deciding when 24 * two owners belong to the same household lives in one place, as pure functions with no web or 25 * persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, which does the same for telephones. 26 * 27 *

Two owners share a household when their {@linkplain #toComparisonKey(String, String) comparison 28 * keys} are equal. ## Summary

I redesigned the owner identity key and duplicate detection to match the specification.

**New `Soundex` utility** (`util/Soundex.java`) — a pure-function implementation of the American Soundex algorithm (first letter + three digits, with vowel/`h`/`w` handling and same-code coalescing), mirroring the existing `TelephoneNormalizer`/`EmailNormalizer` utility style.

**`OwnerIdentity.identityKey`** — now returns `SHA-256 hex over (normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName))`. The third component changed from the household id to the Soundex of the last name, and the whole joined string is now hashed via `Sha256.hex`, so the key is a 64-char lower-case hex digest (satisfying the acceptance test's shape check). The `Owner` overload feeds `lastName` instead of `householdId`.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1`:**
- `rejectDuplicateIdentity` now compares the create's full `identityKey` against every active (non-deleted) owner's `identityKey` and throws `409` on an exact match — the single identity-key rule. The email-domain blocklist still runs first (unchanged, in `normalizeEmail`).
- Removed the separate `rejectHouseholdDuplicate` call and method — the household-duplicate `409` block no longer applies.
- `findPossibleDuplicate` (soft match) now triggers when the `identityKey` differs but `soundex(lastName)` **and** postcode match, returning the oldest such owner. Consequently, two owners sharing last name + postcode but with different telephones now have differing keys and are created as a soft match rather than rejected.

**Removed** the now-dead `DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException` class and its import.

I also updated the Javadoc across the touched classes so the documented behaviour matches the new single-identity-key model.
